G3500.def:
νέκρωσις, -εως, ἡ
(νεκρόω),
__1. a putting to death.
__2. a state of death, death: Rm 4:19, 2Co 4:10 (see Deiss., LAE, 94).†
(AS)

G3501.def:
νέος, -α, -ον
[in LXX for נַעַר (Gn 37:2, Exo_33:11, al.), חָדָשׁ (Lv 23:16, Nm 28:26, al.), etc.; compar. -ώτερος for קָטָן, צָעִיר, etc. ;]
__1. young, youthful: Tt 2:4.
__2. new (prop., in respect of time; see: καινός): οἶνος (cf. οἶ. καινός, Mt 26:20), Mt 9:17, Mc 2:22, Lc 5:37-39; φύραμα (figuratively), 1Co 5:7; διαθήκη (cf. καινὴ δ., Hb 9:15), Hb 12:24; metaphorically, ἄνθρωπος (cf. καινὸς ἀ, Ef 2:15), Cl 3:10.
__3. Compar., -ώτερος, -α, -ον, younger: Lc 15:12-13 22:26, Jo 21:18; pl., οἱ ν., At 5:6 (Rackham, in l), 1Tm 5:11, Tt 2:6; opposite to πρεσβύτεροι, 1Tm 5:1, 1Pe 5:5; αἱ ν., 1Tm 5:2 5:14.
__4. Νέα Πόλις, Neapolis: At 16:11 (Rec., Νεάπολις, which see)
νεώτερος, see: νέος
SYN.: καινός, which see (AS)

G3502.def:
νοσσός (νεοσσός, Rec., as in cl. Att.. -ττός; Phryn. rejects the dissyl. form), -οῦ, ὁ
(νόος), [in LXX chiefly for בֵּן ;]
a young bird: Lc 2:24 (LXX).†
(AS)

G3503.def:
νεότης, -ητος, ἡ
(νέος), [in LXX chiefly for נָעוּר ;]
youth: Mc 10:20, Lc 18:21, At 26:4, 1Tm 4:12.†
(AS)

G3504.def:
νεό-φυτος, -ον
(νέος, φύω) [in LXX: Jó 14:9, Sl 144:12, Is 5:7 (נֶטַע), Sl 128:3 (שְׁתִל)* ;]
newly planted (LXX). Metaphorical, as subst., ὁ ν., a new convert, neophyte, novice: 1Tm 3:6†
(AS)

G3506.def:
νεύω
[in LXX: Pv 4:5 21:1 * ;]
to nod or beckon, as a sign : with dative of person(s) and inf., Jo 13:24, At 24:10 (cf. δια-, ἐκ-, ἐν-, ἐπι-, κατα-νεύω).†
(AS)

G3507.def:
νεφέλη, -ης, ἡ
(νέφος), [in LXX chiefly for עָנָן, also for עָב, etc. ;]
a cloud (single and specific as opposite to νεφος, a great indefinite mass of vapour): Mt 17:5 24:30 26:64, Mc 9:7 13:26 14:62, Lc 9:34-35 12:54 21:37, At 1:9, 1Ts 4:17, Ju 12, Ap 1:7 10:1 11:12 14:14-16; of the pillar of cloud in the wilderness (Êx 14:19-20, Sl 105:39, al.): 1Co 10:1-2.†
(AS)

G3508.def:
Νεφθαλείμ
(-λίμ, WH in Re, l.with), ὁ
indecl. (Heb. נַפְתָּלִי)
Naphtali: Mt 4:13, 15" (LXX) Ap 7:6.†
(AS)

G3509.def:
νέφος, -ους, τό
[in LXX for עָב, שַׁחַק, עָנַן ;]
a mass of clouds, a cloud (cf. νεφέλη); metaphorically as in Hom., Hdt., al.), of a dense throng: Hb 12:1.†
(AS)

G3510.def:
νεφρός, -οῦ, ὁ
[in LXX for כִּלְיָה, Êx 29:13, al.; metaphorically, Sl 7:9 16:7 26:2, Wis.1:6, al. ;]
a kidney; pl., the kidneys, reins; metaphorically, of the will and affections: ν. καί καρδίαι (thoughts), Ap 2:23.†
(AS)

G3511.def:
νεω-κόρος, -ου
a temple-keeper; as honorary title given to a city (see DB, i, 722 b) : At 19:35.†
(AS)

G3512.def:
νεωτερικός, -ή, -όν
(νεώτερος), [in LXX: 3Ma.4:8 * ;]
= νεανικός,
youthful, esp. of qualities: ἐπιθυμίαι, 2Tm 2:22 (Polyb.).†
(AS)

G3513.def:
νή
particle of affirmation employed in oaths, [in LXX: see τ. ὑγίειαν, Gn 42:15-16 (חַי) * ;]
by: with accusative, 1Co 15:31.†
(AS)

G3514.def:
νήθω
[in LXX for טָוָה, שָׁזַר hoph., Êx 26:31 35:25, al. ;]
to spin: Mt 6:28, Lc 12:27.†
(AS)

G3516.def:
νήπιος, -α, -ον
[in LXX chiefly for עוֹלֵל, also for פְּתִי, etc. ;]
infant; of children and minors: Mt 21:16 (LXX), 1Co 13:11, Gl 4:1 (see Lft., in l). Metaphorical, childish, unskilled, simple (Sl 19:8, Pv 1:32 al.): Mt 11:25, Lc 10:21, Rm 2:20, Gl 4:3, Ef 4:14, 1Ts 2:7 (WH, fox ἤπιοι); opposite to τέλειος, Hb 5:13; ν. ἐν Χριστῷ, 1Co 3:1.†
(AS)

G3517.def: Nereus , a sea-god, son of Πόντος (the sea) , father of the Nereids, (Hesiod) (ML)

G3519.def:
νησίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of νῆσος), = νησίς (Hdt., Thuc., al.)
a small island: At 27:16.†
(AS)

G3520.def:
νῆσος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for אִי ;]
an island: At 13:6 27:26 28:1, 7 28:9, 11 Ap 1:9 6:14 16:20.†
(AS)

G3521.def:
νηστεία, -ας, ἡ
(νηστεύω), [in LXX for צוֹם ;]
fasting, a fast;
__(a) of voluntary abstinence from food: Mt 17:21 (WH, R, txt., om.), Mc 9:29 (WH, txt., R, txt., om.), Lc 2:37, At 14:23; of the Day of Atonement, At 27:9;
__(b) of involuntary abstinence: 2Co 6:5 11:27.†
SYN.: ἀσιτία, q.v (AS)

G3522.def:
νηστεύω
(νῆστις), [in LXX for צוּם ;]
to fast (Arist., Aristoph., al.): Mt 4:2 6:16-18 9:14-15 Mc 2:18-20, Lc 5:33-35 18:12, At 13:2-3.†
(AS)

G3523.def:
νῆστις, -ιος, ὁ, ἡ
(νη-, neg. prefix, + ἐσθίω),
in cl., chiefly poët.,
[in LXX: Dan LXX 6:18 (19) (טְוָת)* ;]
not eating, fasting: Mt 15:32, Mc 8:3.†
(AS)

G3524.def:
νηφάλιος (-λεος, Rec., in 1Ti, ll. with), -ον (in cl., -α, -ον),
(νήφω),
__1. in cl., of drink, not mixed with wine.
__2. In later writers (Plut., al.), of persons, sober, temperate: 1Tm 3:2 3:11, Tt 2:2.†
(AS)

G3525.def:
νήφω
to be sober, abstain from wine; metaphorically, of moral alertness, to be sober, calm, circumspect: 1Ts 5:6 5:8, 2Tm 4:5 (see Ellic., in l), 1Pe 1:13 4:7 5:8 (cf. ἐκ-, ἐκ-νήφω, and see MM, xvii).†
SYN.: ἀγρυπνέω, γρηγορέω (AS)

G3528.def:
νικἀω, -ῶ
(νίκη), [in LXX: Sl 51:4 (זָכָה), Pv 6:25 frequently (חָמַד); in 4Mac ;]
to conquer, prevail: absol., of Christ, Ap 3:21 6:2; C. inf., Ap 5:5; of Christians, Ap 2:7, 11 2:17, 26 3:5, 12 3:21 21:7; before ἐκ (RV, come victorious from), Ap 15:2; as law-term (cl.), Rm 3:4 (LXX); with accusative of person(s), Lc 11:22, Ap 11:7 13:7 ([WH], R, mg., om.); of Christ, Jo 16:33 (τ. κόσμον), Ap 17:14; of Christians, 1Jo 4:4; τ. πονηρόν, 1Jo 2:13-14; αὐτόν (ref. to ὁ κατήγωρ, 1Jo 2:10), Ap 12:11; with accusative of thing(s), τὸν κόσμον, Jo 16:33, 1Jo 5:4-5; τὸ κακόν, Rm 12:21; pass., μὴ νικῶ ὑπὸ τ. κακοῦ, ib. (cf. ὑπερ-νικάω).†
(AS)

G3533.def:
Νικόπολις, -εως, ἡ
Nicopolis, prob. the city of that name in Epirus (CGT, in l): Tt 3:12†
(AS)

G3534.def:
νῖκος, -ους, τό late form of νίκη,
[in LXX: La 3:18 (נֶצַח), I Et 3:9, 2Ma.10:38, 4Ma.17:12; εἰς ν. (instead of εἰς τέλος, Jó 14:20), 2Rs 2:26, Jó 36:7, Am 1:11 8:7, Jr 3:5, La 5:20 (נֶצַח, as נ֝ in Syr., = victory)* ;]
victory: Mt 12:20 (Is 42:3, LXX ἀλήθεια), 1Co 15:54 (Is 25:8, Aq., Th.), 1Co 15:55 (Os 13:14, LXX δίκη), 1Co 15:57.†
(AS)

G3538.def:
νίπτω late form of νίζω,
[in LXX chiefly for רָחַץ ;]
to wash, usually of a part of the body: with accusative of person(s), Jo 13:8; τ. πόδας, Jo 13:5-6, 8 13:12, 14, 1Tm 5:10; mid., reflexive,
to wash oneself: Jo 9:7, 11 9:15; τ. χεῖρας, Mt 15:2, Mc 7:3; τ. πόδας, Jo 13:10; τ. πρόσωπον, Mt 6:17 (in cl. Att.. prose, used only in compounds; cf. ἀπο-νίπτω).†
νίζω, see: νίπτω
SYN.: λούω (which see), πλύνω (AS)

G3539.def:
νοιεω νοέω, -ῶ
(νοῦς), [in LXX chiefly for בִּין, also for שָׂכַל hi., etc ;]
__1. to perceive with the mind, understand (for the phrase νοῶν κ. φρονῶν, in wills, see MM, xvii): absol., Mt 16:9, Mc 8:17; with accusative, Ef 3:4, 1Tm 1:7; with dative instr., τ. καρδίᾳ, Jo 12:40; pass., Rm 1:20; before ὅτι, Mt 15:17 16:11, Mc 7:18; with accusative and inf., Hb 11:8.
__2. to think, consider: absol., Mt 24:15, Mc 13:14, Ef 3:20; with accusative of thing(s), 2Tm 2:7
(cf. -εὐ, κατα-, μετα-, προ-, ὑπο-νοέω).†
(AS)

G3540.def:
νόημα, -τος, τό
(νοέω) [in LXX: Sir.21:11, Bar.2:8, 3Ma.5:30 * ;]
a thought, purpose, design: 2Co 2:11 10:5 11:3, Fp 4:7. Meton., of the mind, 2Co 3:14 4:4.†
(AS)

G3541.def:
νόθος, -η, -ον
[in LXX: Wis.4:3 * ;]
a bastard, base born, i.e. born of a slave or concubine: Hb 12:8.†
(AS)

G3542.def:
νομή, -ῆς, ἡ
(νέμω, to pasture), [in LXX chiefly for מִרְעֶה, also for נָוֶה, etc. ;]
__1. a pasture, pasturage: figuratively, Jo 10:9
__2. a grazing, feeding; metaphorically, of a spreading sore, 2Tm 2:17 (Polyb.).†
(AS)

G3543.def:
νομίζω
(νόμος), [in LXX: Wis.13:2 17:3, Sir.29:4, 1-28; 2Ma.4:1-50, 4Ma.8:1-29 * ;]
__1. to practise, hold by custom: At 16:13 (Rec., but see infr.).
__2. to deem, consider, suppose: Mt 5:17 10:34 20:10, Lc 2:44 3:23, At 7:25 8:20 14:19 16:13, 27 17:29 21:29, 1Co 7:26 7:36, 1Tm 6:5.†
SYN.: ἡγέομαι, q.v (AS)

G3544.def:
νομικός, -ή, -όν
(νόμος), [in LXX: 4Ma.5:4 * ;]
__1. relating to law: μάχαι, Tt 3:9.
__2. learned in the law; as subst., ὁ ν. (EV, lawyer): Mt 22:35, Lc 10:25, Tt 3:13; pl., Lc 7:30 11:45-46, 52 14:3 (cf. MM, xvii).†
SYN.: γραμματεύς, q.v (AS)

G3546.def:
νόμισμα, -τος, τό
(νομίζω), [in LXX: Et 8:36 (דָּת), Ne 7:71 R (דַּרְכְּמוֹן), 1Ma.15:6 * ;]
__1. that which is established by usage, a custom.
__2. The current coin of a state: Mt 22:19.†
(AS)

G3547.def:
νομο-διδάσκαλος, -ου, ὁ
a teacher of the law: Lc 5:17, At 5:34, 1Tm 1:7 (NT and eccl. only; cf. νομοδείκτης, -διδάκτης, Plut.).†
SYN.: γραμματεύς, q.v (AS)

G3549.def:
νομοθετέω, -ῶ
[in LXX for יָרָה hi. ;]
__1. intrans., to make laws; pass., to be furnished with laws: Hb 7:11.
__2. Trans., to ordain by law, enact: pass., Hb 8:6.†
(AS)

G3550.def:
νομο-θέτης, -ου, ὁ
(νόμος, τίθημι), [in LXX: Sl 9:20 * ;]
a law­giver: Tg 4:12.†
(AS)

G3551.def:
νόμος, -ου, ὁ
(νέμω, to deal out, distribute), [in LXX chiefly for תּוֹרָה, also for חֻקָּה, etc. ;]
that which is assigned, hence, usage, custom, then law; in NT (only in Mt, Jo, Ja, and the Lucan and Pauline bks.);
__1. of law in general: Rm 3:27 5:13b; pl., of divine laws, Hb 8:10 10:16; ὁ ν. τ. Χριστοῦ, Gl 6:2; (τ.) ἐλευθερίας, Tg 1:25 2:12; βασιλικιός (Hort., in l.; Deiss., LAE, 267:3), Tg 2:8.
__2. Of a force or influence impelling to action: Rm 7:21, 23a, 25 8:2.
__3. Of the Mosaic law: Mt 5:18, Lc 2:27, Jo 1:17, At 6:13, Rm 2:15, 1Co 9:8, 1Tm 1:8, Hb 7:19; al.; Μωυσέως, Lc 2:22, Jo 7:23, At 15:5, al.; κυρίου, Lc 2:39; κατὰ τὸν ν., At 22:12, Hb 7:5 9:22.
__4. As printed, Abbott-Smith mistakenly numbers this as 3.Anarthrous (Bl, §46, 8; ICC on Rm 2:12, 13), νόμος,
__(a) of law in general: Rm 2:12, 14b 3:20, 21 4:15, al.;
__(b) of the Mosaic law in its quality as law: Rm 2:14a 5:20 10:4, Gl 2:19, al.; οἱ ἐκ ν., Rm 4:14; ὑπὸ νόμον, 1Co 9:20, Gl 4:5; ν. πράσσειν (πληροῦν), Rm 2:25 13:8.
__5. Of Christian teaching: ν. πίστεως, Rm 3:27; τ. Χριστοῦ, Gl 6:2.
__6. By meton., of the books which contain the law;
__(a) of the Pentateuch: Mt 12:5, Jo 1:45, al.; ὁ ν. καὶ οἱ προφῆται, Mt 5:17, Lc 16:16, al.; ὁ ν. καὶ προφῆται κ. ψαλμοί, Lc 24:44.
__(b) of the OT Scriptures in general (as Heb. תּוֹרָה): Jo 10:34 12:34 15:25, 1Co 14:21, al.
(AS)

G3552.def:
νοσέω, -ῶ
(νόσος), [in LXX (metaphorically): Wis.17:8 * ;]
to be sick: metaphorically, of mental ailment, before περί, 1Tm 6:4 (cf. Plat., Mor., 546 d).†
(AS)

G3554.def:
νόσος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for חֲלִי, etc. ;]
disease, sickness: Mt 4:23-24 8:17 (Aq.) Mt 9:35 10:1, Mc 1:34, Lc 4:40 6:17 7:21 9:1, At 19:12.†
SYN.: see: ἀσθένεια (AS)

G3555.def:
νοσσιά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(νοσσός),
late form of cl., νεοσσιά,
[in LXX chiefly for קֵן ;]
__1. a nest of birds.
__2. a brood of young birds: Lc 13:34.†
(AS)

G3556.def:
νοσσίον, -ου, τό dimin. of νοσσός, which see,
[in LXX: Sl 84:3 (אֶפְרֹחַ) * ;]
a young bird: Mt 23:37.†
(AS)

G3557.def:
νοσφίζω
(νόσφι, apart, aside), [in LXX: Js 7:1 (לָקַח), 2Ma.4:32 * ;]
__1. in Hom., as depon., to turn away (from), abandon.
__2. After Hom., in act., to set apart, remove. Mid., to set apart for oneself, peculate, purloin: absol., Tt 2:10 (for ex. in π., see MM, xvii); before ἀπό, At 5:2-3.†
(AS)

G3558G.def:
νότος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for נֶגֶב, also for דָּרוֹם, תֵּימָן and קָדִים ;]
__1. prop., the south wind: Lc 12:55, At 27:13 28:13
__2. South: Lc 13:29, Ap 21:13
__3. the South, as a region (cf. נֶגֶב): Mt 12:42, Lc 11:31.†
(AS)

G3558H.def:
νότος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for נֶגֶב, also for דָּרוֹם, תֵּימָן and קָדִים ;]
__1. prop., the south wind: Lc 12:55, At 27:13 28:13
__2. South: Lc 13:29, Ap 21:13
__3. the South, as a region (cf. נֶגֶב): Mt 12:42, Lc 11:31.†
(AS)

G3559.def:
νουθεσία, -ας ἡ
(νουθετέω),
= cl. νουθέτησις
[in LXX: Wis.6:6 * ;]
admonition: 1Co 10:11, Ef 6:4, Tt 3:10 (Aristoph., Diod., al.).†
(AS)

G3560.def:
νουθετέω, -ῶ
(νοῦς, τίθημι, hence, put in mind), [in LXX: 1Rs 3:13 (כָּהָה pi.), Jó 8:1-22 (יָסַר pi., בִּין), Wis.11:10 12:2, 26 * ;]
to admonish, exhort: with accusative of person(s), At 20:31, Rm 15:14, 1Co 4:14, Cl 1:28 3:16, 1Ts 5:12 5:14, 2Ts 3:15.†
(AS)

G3561.def:
νεομηνία (Att.. contr., νουμ-, Rec.), -ας, ἡ
(νέος, μήν), [in LXX chiefly for חֹדֶשׁ ;]
new moon: of the Jewish festival, Cl 2:16.†
(AS)

G3563.def:
νοῦς
(contr. from νόος), ὁ, genitive, dative, νοός, νοΐ (late forms, = cl., νοῦ, νῷ; Bl., § 9, 3), accusative, νοῦν, [in LXX chiefly for לֵב, לֵבָב ;]
__1. prop., of the ruling faculty, mind, understanding, reason (see Lft., Notes, 88 f.; Vaughan on Rm 7:23): Lc 24:45, Rm 1:28 7:23 12:2 14:5, Ef 4:17, 23 Fp 4:7, 2Ts 2:2, 1Tm 6:5, 2Tm 3:8, Tt 1:15, Ap 13:18 17:9; ν. τ. σαρκός (ICC, in l), Cl 2:18; opposite to σάρξ, Rm 7:25; to πνεῦμα, 1Co 14:14-15; to γλῶσσα, 1Co 14:19
__2. By meton., of an act of mind, a mind, thought, purpose: Rm 11:34 = 1Co 2:16" (LXX), 1Co 1:10.†
νόος, see: νοῦς
SYN.: see: πνεῦμα (AS)

G3564.def:
Νυμφᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ (WH, R, mg., Νύμφα, which see),
Nymphas: Cl 4:15, R, txt. (cf. ICC, Lft., in l).†
Νύμφα (Rec., R, txt., Νυμφᾶς, which see), -ης, ἡ, Nympha (see M, Pr., 48): Cl 4:15, WH, R, mg.†
(AS)

G3565.def:
νύμφη, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for כַּלָּה ;]
__1. cl., a bride, young wife, young woman: Mt 25:1, WH, mg., Jo 3:29, Ap 18:23 21:2, 9 22:17.
__2. As frequently in LXX (Gn 38:11, al., for כַּלָּה;
__(a) bride;
__(b) daughter-in-law) and in MGr. (νύφφη, νύφη), a daughter-in-law: Mt 10:35, Lc 12:53.†
(AS)

G3566.def:
νυμφίος, -ου, ὁ
(νύμφη), [in LXX for חָתָן ;]
a bridegroom: Mt 9:15 25:1, 5-6 25:10, Mc 2:19-20, Lc 5:34-35, Jo 2:9 3:29, Ap 18:23.†
(AS)

G3567.def:
νυμφών, -ῶνος, ὁ
(νύμφη), [in LXX: Tob.6:13,16* ;]
the bride-chamber (Heb. חֻפָּה, LXX, παστός, Sl 19:5, Jl 2:16): Mt 22:10 (WE; γάμος, RV); οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ ν. (cf. cl. νυμφαγωγός, νυμφευτής), the bridegroom's friends who have charge of the nuptial arrangements: Mt 9:15, Mc 2:19, Lc 5:34.†
(AS)

G3568.def:
νῦν, adv.,
[in LXX chiefly for עַתָּה ;]
__1. prop., of time, now, i.e. at the present time: as opposite to past, Jo 4:18, At 7:52, Rm 13:11, 2Co 7:9, Cl 1:24, al.; opposite to fut., Jo 12:27, Rm 11:31, al.; with art., ὁ (ἡ, τὸ) and subst., the present: Rm 3:26, Gl 4:25, 1Tm 6:17, Tt 2:12, al.; απὸ τοῦ ν. (LXX for מֵעַתָּה), Lc 1:48, At 18:6, al.; ἄχρι τοῦ ν., Rm 8:22, Fp 1:5; ἕως τοῦ ν. (LXX for עַד עַתָּה), Mt 24:21, Mc 13:19; τὰ ν., as regards the present, At 5:38; with pret., just now, but now, Mt 26:65, Jo 11:8 21:10; with fut., now, presently, Jo 12:31, At 20:22; so with praes., presently, forthwith, Jo 12:31 17:13; καὶ ν., Jo 11:22 17:5, al.; ἀλλὰ ν., Lc 22:36; ἔτι ν., 1Co 3:2; τότε (πότε) . . . ν. (δέ), Rm 6:21 11:30; ν. ἤδη, 1Jo 4:3; ν. οὖν, At 10:33, al.
__2. Of logical sequence (often difficult to disting. from the temporal sense; cf. Lft., Notes, 113f.), now, therefore, now, however, as it is: Lc 11:39; καὶ ν., At 3:17, 2Ts 2:6, 1Jo 2:28; id. before δεῦρο, At 7:34; ν. δέ, Jo 8:40 9:41 15:22, 24, 18:36, 1Co 5:11 7:14 12:20, al. (cf. WM, 579.11).
(AS)

G3570.def:
νῦνί an Attic strengthened form of νῦν
(in cl. always of time, and most often strictly of the pres.), [in LXX : Jó 5:1-27, Sl 2:1-12, 1-12, 4Ma.4:1-26, Ep. Je* ;]
now;
__1. of time: with praes., At 24:13, Rm 15:23, 25, 1Co 13:13, 2Co 8:11 8:22, Phm 9 11; with pf., Rm 3:21; with pret., Rm 6:22 11:30 (WH, mg.) Rm 7:6, Ef 2:13, Cl 1:21 3:8; ἡ ν. ἀπολογία, At 22:1.
__2. Of logical sequence (not so in cl.): Rm 7:17, 1Co 5:11 (νῦν, WH) 1Co 12:18 (νῦν, WH, txt.) 1Co 15:20, Hb 8:6 (νῦν, WH, txt.), Hb 9:26 (cf. WM, 24, 579n).†
(AS)

G3571.def:
νύξ genitive νυκτός, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for לַיִל ;]
night: Mt 12:40, Mc 6:48, Jo 13:30, al.; genitive temp. (of the time within which something happens; M, Pr., 73; B1., § 36, 13), νυκτός, by night, Mt 2:14, Jo 3:2, 1Ts 5:7, al.; ν. κ. ἡμέρας, Mc 5:5, 1Ts 2:9, al.; ἡμέρας κ. ν., Lc 18:7, Ap 4:8, al.; μέσης ν., Mt 25:6; dative, νυκτί, in ans. to the question, "when?" (rare in cl.; Hdt., Soph.), ταύτῃ τ. ν., Lc 12:20, al.; ἐκείνῃ At 12:6; ἐπιούσῃ, At 23:11; accusative durat. (Bl., § 34, 8; Kühner3, III, 314b), ν. κ. ἠμέραν, Lc 2:37 At 20:31; τ. νύκτας, Lc 21:37; διὰ νυκτός (= cl. νυκτός; Bl., § 42, 1; 46, 7), At 5:19 16:9 17:10 23:31; δι᾽ ὅλης ν., Lc 5:5; κατὰ μέσον τῆς ν. (Bl., § 47, 6), At 27:27. Metaphorical: Jo 9:4, Rm 13:12, 1Ts 5:5
(AS)

G3572.def:
νύσσω
(Att.. -ττω), [in LXX: Sir.22:19, 3Ma.5:14 * ;]
to pierce: τ. πλευρὰν λόγχῃ, Jo 19:34, [Mt 27:49], WH.†
(AS)

G3573.def:
νυστάζω
(cf. νεύω), [in LXX for נוּם, etc ;]
to nod in sleep, fall asleep: Mt 25:5. Metaphorical, of negligence or delay, ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτῶν οὐ νυστάζει (cf. Sl 121:4, Is 5:27) : 2Pe 2:3.†
(AS)

G3574.def:
νυχθήμερος, -α, -ον
(νύξ, ἡμέρα, see B1., § 28, 4),
lasting a night and a day; as subst., (τὸ) ν., a night and a day: 2Co 11:25 (pl., Or. Sib., 8, 203).†
(AS)

G3575.def:
Νῶε
(as LXX, FlJ, who also gives Νώεος, Νῶχος), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נֹחַ)
Noah: Mt 24:37-38, Lc 3:36 17:26-27 Hb 11:7, 1Pe 3:20, 2Pe 2:5.†
(AS)

G3576.def:
νωθρός, -ά, -όν
[in LXX: Pv 22:29 (חָשֹׁךְ), Sir.4:29 11:12 * ;]
sluggish, slothful: Hb 5:11 6:12 (for similar usage in π., see MM, xvii).
SYN.: ἀργός (which see), βραδύς (AS)

G3577.def:
νῶτος, -ου, ὁ
in Att.. most frequently τὸ νῶτον, and in pl. always τὰ νῶτα, [in LXX, ὁ ν., pl., οἱ νῶτοι and τὰ νῶτα, chiefly for כָּתֵף, also for עֹרֶף, מֹתֶן ;]
/the back: Rm 11:10 (LXX).†
(AS)

G3578.def:
ξενία, -ας, ἡ
(ξένος), [in LXX: Sir.29:27 Bl* ;]
hospitality, enter­tainment: Phm 22 (cf. ICC, in l, but see infr.). By meton., a place of entertainment, a lodging-place: At 28:23, and so perh. Phm 22 (Lft., in l, Phi., p. 9; but see supr., and cf. MM, xvii).†
(AS)

G3579.def:
ξενίζω
(ξένος), [in LXX: Et 3:13, Sir.29:25, 2Ma.9:6, 3Ma.7:3 * ;]
__1. to receive as a guest, entertain: with accusative of person(s), At 10:23 28:7, Hb 13:2; pass., At 10:6, 18 10:32 21:16.
__2. In late writers (Polyb., al.; 2Mac, l.with), to surprise, astonish by strangeness: At 17:20; pass., 1Pe 4:4 4:12.†
(AS)

G3580.def:
ξενοδοχέω late Gk. for -κέω
(ξένος, δέχομαι),
to entertain strangers: 1Tm 5:10.†
(AS)

G3581.def:
ξένος, -η, -ον
[in LXX chiefly for נׇכְרִי ;]
__(a) foreign, alien: δαιμόνια, At 17:18; διδαχαί Hb 13:9;
__(b) with genitive of thing(s), strange to, estranged from, ignorant of: Ef 2:12;
__(with) strange, unusual: 1Pe 4:12.
As subst., ὁ ξ.,
__(a) a foreigner, stranger: Mt 25:35, 38 25:43-44 27:7, At 17:21, 3Jn.5; ξέίνοι κ. τάροικοι (opposite to συμπολῖται, οίκεῖοι), Ef 2:19; ξ. καὶ παρεπίδημοι, Hb 11:13;
__(b) one of the parties bound by ties of hospitality;
__α the guest;
__β the host (= ξενοδόκος, Hom., Ii, xv, 532) : Rm 16:23.†
(AS)

G3582.def:
ξέστης, -ου, ὁ
(a Sicilian corruption of Lat. sextarius), [in Al. : Lv 14:10 (לֹג, LXX κοτύλη)* ;]
__1. a sextarius (about a pint).
__2. In NT, a pitcher of wood or stone : Mc 7:4.†
(AS)

G3583.def:
ξηραίνω
(ξηρός), [in LXX chiefly for יָבֵשׁ ;]
to dry up, parch, wither. with accusative, τ. χόρτον, Tg 1:11; pass., to become or be dry or withered. of plants, Mt 13:6 21:19-20, Mc 4:6 11:20-21, Lc 8:6, Jo 15:6, 1Pe 1:24; of ripened crops, Ap 14:15; of liquids, Mc 5:20, Ap 16:12; of members of the body, to waste away, Mc 3:1 (cf. 3Ki.13:4) Mc 9:18.†
(AS)

G3584.def:
ξηρός, -ά, -όν
[in LXX chiefly for יָבֵשׁ, its parts and deriva­tives, also for חָרָבָה, etc. ;]
dry: metaphorically (of a sinner), ξύλον ξ., Lc 23:31; of members of the body shrunken by disease, withered: Jo 5:3; of the hand, Mt 12:10 Mc 3:3, Lc 6:6, 8; of the dry land, ἡ ξηρά (sc. γῆ, cf. Gn 1:9-10; Jn 1:19, al.): Mt 23:15; γῆ, Hb 11:29.†
(AS)

G3585.def:
ξύλινος, -η, -ον
(ξύλον) [in LXX chiefly for עֵץ ;]
wooden: 2Tm 2:20, Hb 9:20 (cf. Ep. Jr 4:1-31 ff).†
(AS)

G3586.def:
ξύλον, -ου, τό
[in LXX chiefly for עֵץ ;]
__1. wood: 1Co 3:12, Ap 18:12.
__2. a piece of wood, hence, anything made of wood, as,
__(a) a cudgel, staff: pl., Mt 26:47, 55, Mc 14:43, 48, Lc 22:52;
__(b) stocks, for confining the feet (Jó 33:11, סַד) : At 16:24;
__(with) a beam to which malefactors were bound (late Gk.), in LXX, of a gibbet (Dt 21:22-23), in NT, of the Cross: At 5:30 10:39 13:29, Gl 3:13, 1Pe 2:24.
__3. In late writers (see MM, xvii), a tree (Gn 1:29, Is 14:8, al.) : Lc 23:31; ξ. τῆς ζωῆς, Ap 2:7 22:2, 14 22:19.†
(AS)

G3587.def:
ξυράω, -ῶ
late form of ξυρέω (which see) : 1Co 11:6 (ξυρᾶσθαι, Rec. and Edd., but see: ξύρω).†
ξύρω, rare form of ξυρέω (Veitch, see word), aor. mid., ξύρασθαιι (Bl., § 24, see word; Zorell, see word, etc.) for -ᾶσθαι (Rec., Edd.) : 1Co 11:6.†
(AS)

G3588.def:
ὁ, ἡ, τό,
the prepositive article (ἄρθρον προτακτικόν), originally a demonstr. pron. (so usually in Hom.), in general corresponding to the Eng. definite article.
__I. As demonstr. pron.
__1. As frequently in Hom., absol., he (she, it), his (etc.): At 17:28 (quoted from the poet Aratus).
__2. Distributive, ὁ μὲν . . . ὁ δέ, the one . . . the other: 1Co 7:7, Gl 4:22; pl., At 14:4, 17:32, Fp 1:16, al.; οἱ μὲν . . . ἄλλοι δέ, Mt 16:14, Jo 7:12; οἱ μεν̀ . . . ὁδέ, Hb 7:21, 23.
__3. In narration (without ὁ μὲν preceding), ὁ δέ, but he: Mt 2:14, Mc 1:45, Lc 8:21, Jo 9:38, al. mult.
__II. As prepositive article, the, prefixed,
__1. to nouns unmodified: ὁ θεός, τὸ φῶς, etc.; to abstract nouns, ἡ σοφία, etc., to pl. nouns which indicate a class, οἱ ἀλώπεκες, foxes, Mt 8:20, al.; to an individual as representing a class, ὁ ἐργάτης, Lc 10:7; with nom. = voc. in addresses, Mt 11:26, Jo 19:3, Tg 5:1, al.; to things which pertain to one, ἡ χεῖρ, his hand, Mc 3:1; to names of persons well known or already mentioned; usually to names of countries (originally adjectives), ἡ Ἰουδαία, etc.
__2. To modified nouns: with of person(s) pron. genitive, μοῦ, σοῦ, etc.; with poss. pron., ἐμός, σός, etc.; with adj. between the art. and the noun, ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος, Mt 12:35; the noun foll, by adj., both with art., ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός, Jo 10:11 (on ὁ ὄχλος πολύς, Jo 12:9, see M, Pr., 84); before adjectival phrases, ἡ κατ᾽ ἐκλογὴν πρόθεσις, Rm 9:11.
__3. To Other parts of speech used as substantives;
__(a) neuter adjectives: τ. ἀγαθόν, etc.;
__(b) cardinal numerals: ὁ εἶς, οἷ δύο, etc.;
__(with) participles: ὁ βαπτίζων (= ὁ Βαπτιστής, Mt 14:2), Mc 6:14; πᾶς ὁ, with ptcp., every one who, etc.;
__(d) adverbs: τὸ πέραν, τὰ νῦν, ὁ ἔσω ἄνθρωπος;
__(e) infinitives: nom., τὸ θέλειν, Rm 7:18, al.; genitive, τοῦ, after adjectives, ἄξιον τοῦ πορεύεσθαι, 1Co 16:4; verbs, ἐλαχεν τοῦ θυμιᾶσαι, Lc 1:9; and frequently in a final sense, ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρειν, Mt 13:3 (on the artic. inf., see Bl., §71).
__4. In the neut. to sentences, phrases or single words treated as a quotation: τὸ Ἐι δύνῃ, Mc 9:23; τὸ ἔτι ἅπαξ, Hb 12:27; τὸ ἀνέβη, Ef 4:9, al.
__5. To prepositional phrases: οἱ ἀπὸ Ἰταλίας, Hb 13:24; οἱ ἐκ νόμου, Rm 4:14; neut. accusative absol., in adverbial phrases, τὸ καθ᾽ ἡμέραν, daily, Lc 11:3; τὸ κατὰ σάρκα, as regards the flesh, Rm 9:5.
__6. To nouns in the genitive, denoting kinship, association, etc.: ὁ τοῦ, the son of (unless context indicates a different relationship), Mt 10:2, al.; τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ, the things that pertain to God, Mt 16:23; τὰ τῆς εἰρήνης, Rm 14:19 (cf. M, Pr., 81ff.; Bl, §§46, 47).
(AS)

G3589.def: eighty , Lat. octoginta, (Thucydides), etc.:—;ionic and doric ὀγδώκοντα, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G3590.def:
ὄγδοος, -η, -ον
the eighth. Lc 1:59, At 7:3" (LXX), Ap 17:11 21:20; one of eight, with seven others (usually, in this sense, with αὐτός added, but cf. Plat., Legg., iii, 695 with; Plut., Pelop., 13; 2Ma.5:27): 2Pe 2:5.†
(AS)

G3591.def:
ὄγκος, -ου, ὁ
bulk, mass; metaphorically, an encumbrance: Hb 12:1.†
SYN.: βάρος, a weight; φορτίον, a burden, that which is borne (AS)

G3592.def:
ὅδε, ἥδε, τόδε
(the old demonstr. pron., ὁ + the enclitic δε), = Lat. hicce, this (here),
referring prop, to what is present, can be seen or pointed out: of a person just named, τῇδε (= ταύτῃ), Lc 10:39; neut. pl., τάδε (λέγει), referring to words which follow (so in Att.., and see MM, xvii) : At 21:11, Ap 2:1, 8 2:12, 18 3:1, 7 3:14; εἰς τήνδε τ. πόλιν (= Att.. τῇ καὶ τῇ, Plat., Legg., iv, 721 B), such and such a city, Tg 4:13.†
(AS)

G3593.def:
ὁδεύω
(ὁδός), [in LXX : 3Ki.6:12 A (metaphorically, הָלַךְ), Tob.6:5, Wis.5:7 (figuratively)* ;]
to travel, journey: Lc 10:33 (cf.δι-, συν-οδεύω).†
(AS)

G3594.def:
ὁδηγέω, -ῶ,
(ὁδηγός) [in LXX chiefly for נוּחַ, also for דֶּרֶךְ hi., הָלַךְ hi., etc. ;]
to lead on one's way, to guide: with accusative of person(s), Mt 15:14, Lc 6:39; id. before ἐπί, Ap 7:17. Metaphorical, to guide, instruct, teach: At 8:31; before εἰς τ. ἀλήθειαν (ἐν τ. ἀ., WH, mg.), Jo 16:13 (cf. Sl 25:5).†
(AS)

G3595.def:
ὁδηγός, -οῦ, ὁ
(ὁδός, ἡγέομαι) [in LXX : Et 8:1, Wis.7:15 18:3, 1Ma.4:2, 2Ma.5:15 * ;]
a leader on the way, a guide: At 1:16. Fig., ὁ. τυφλῶν, Rm 2:19; pl., Mt 15:14 23:16, 24.†
(AS)

G3596.def:
ὁδοιπορέω, -ῶ
(ὁδοιπόρος, a traveller, Gn 37:25, al.),
to travel, journey: At 10:9.†
(AS)

G3597.def:
ὁδοιπορία, -ας, ἡ
(see supr.), [in LXX : Wis.13:18 18:3 19:5, 1Ma.6:41 * ;]
a journey. Jo 4:6, 2Co 11:26.†
(AS)

G3598.def:
ὁδός, -οῦ, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly (very freq.) for דֶּרֶךְ ;]
__1. a way, path, road: Mt 2:12, Mc 10:46, Lc 3:5 al.; κατὰ τὴν ὁ., Lc 10:4, al.; παρὰ τὴν ὁ., Mt 13:4, al.; with genitive of person(s), (subj.), τὴν ὁ. ἑτοιμάζειν (fig.), Mt 3:3, Mc 1:3, al.; with genitive term. (obj.), ἐθνῶν, Mt 10:5; τ. ἁγίων (figuratively), Hb 9:8; accusative, ὁδόν, with force of prep. (like Heb. דֶּרֶךְ; Bl., §34, 8; 35, 5), ὁ. θαλάσσης, Mt 4:15 (LXX).
__2. A traveller's way, journey: ἐν τ. ὁ., Mt 5:25, Mc 8:27, al.; ἐξ ὁ., Lc 11:6; εἰς ὁ., Mt 10:10; τ. ὁδὸν πορεύεσθαι, At 8:39; ὁ. ἡμέρας, Lc 2:44; ὁδὸν ποιεῖν (= cl., ὁ. ποιεῖσθαι; V. Field, Notes, 25), to make one's way, i.e. proceed on one's journey, Mc 2:23.
__3. Metaphorical (cl.; but esp. frequently in Heb.; see Cremer, 442ff.), of a course of conduct, a way of thinking or acting: At 14:16, 1Co 4:17 12:31, Tg 1:8 5:20; τοῦ Κάϊν, Ju 11; τ. Βαλαάμ, 2Pe 2:15; εἰρήνης, Rm 3:17; ζωῆς, At 2:28; ἡ ὁ. ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τ. ζωήν (Dalman, Words, 160), Mt 7:14; τ. δικαιοσύνης, Mt 21:32; σωτηρίας, At 16:17; αἱ ὁ. τ. θεοῦ (κυρίου), At 13:10, Rm 11:33, Ap 15:3 (cf. Os 14:9 Psa.94 (95):10, Sir.39:24, al.); ἡ ὁ. τ. θεοῦ (the way approved by God), Mt 22:16, Mc 12:14, Lc 20:21; id., of the Christian religion, At 18:26; so, absol., ἡ ὁ., At 9:2 19:9, 23 24:22; of Christ as the means of approach to God, Jo 14:6.
__4. Ellipsis of ὁ.: ποίας (sc. ὁδοῦ), Lc 5:19; ἐκείνης, ib. 19:4 (see Bl., §36, 13; 44, 1).
(AS)

G3599.def:
ὀδούς, -όντος, ὁ
[in LXX for שֵׁן ;]
a tooth: Mt 5:38, Mc 9:18, At 7:54; pl., Ap 9:8, ὁ βρυγμὸς (which see) τ. ὀδόντων, Mt 8:12 13:42, 50 22:13 24:51 25:30, Lc 13:28.†
(AS)
